design.name: One conversation, one canvas
design.principle: AnA has exactly one place: the conversation. What she builds appears beside her, on the right, in the canvas. That is where the person reads, edits, signs, files and downloads it. Every other screen is a place to work. Its buttons do their job, and when a button needs AnA it brings the work to her with its context and offers a way back. Nothing that already works is rebuilt. The D2 canvas lane's editor beside the conversation (78aef41a, 870edc42, 52697e0c, cf4aa780, 4c8b5534, f822dba1, c2f17977, 9b4fd069, 03ea3dc76) is the canvas. This design makes it open by default, makes it the only right-hand column in the product, and makes the conversation the destination of every ask. The series moves launch row D2 under Rule 2, and each slice files evidence under docs/evidence/D2-ONE-ANA/<date>/. One lane owns the whole series so that the shell stops being edited by 57 sessions at once.
design.layout:
SHELL, ALL SCREENS: left nav | page. The third grid column (--ana 380px open, --ana-seam 32px collapsed; app-v2.css:30-31, 1370-1375) is removed. Every screen gets the full width, and no screen has a right-hand AnA column.

1. AnA CONVERSATION (`conversation-thread`; Home is its empty state)
- Desktop, canvas closed:
  - nav 264px | the conversation as a centred reading column, max 768px.
  - Header: title, a "Working in ONC-221" project chip, "Back to <origin screen>" when the person arrived from a screen, the existing Step chip, and New conversation.
  - Then the transcript, and the composer pinned at the bottom (attach, @app, engine, Live Drive, Between steps).
  - There is no side column. The Progress dock (AnaWorkPanel) opens as a popover from the Step chip.
- Desktop, canvas open:
  - Below 1600px the nav collapses to 56px on its own; a collapse the person chose stays as they set it.
  - Conversation width is clamp(380px, 38%, 560px), then a 1px divider, then the canvas takes the rest.
  - At 1440: 56 | about 526 | about 858. The editor page is about 614px after its 220px outline, against about 530px today.
  - At 1920: 264 | 560 | about 1096.
  - A draggable divider, with the ratio remembered per person, is a later S slice.
- Canvas anatomy:
  - A thin header: "← Documents (n)", title, status pill (Draft / In review / Frozen / Approved), version, project, "⤢ Full screen", "× Close".
  - Under it, the one DocumentWorkbench: outline | section editor | side tabs.
  - Document actions appear once, in the workbench toolbar: Download ▾, File to vault, Assign review, Place into filing, Freeze / E-sign, plus the side tabs (comments, history, sources, signatures, audit, project files, tasks).
  - In its list state the canvas shows "Documents" with a scope switch: "This conversation · This project".
- 1100px and narrower:
  - An open canvas is a full-width sheet over the conversation, and its header reads "← Conversation".
  - An ask from the editor closes the sheet and prefills the composer (existing canvasAsk, ConversationThread.tsx:976-981).
- 760px and narrower: the same, with the nav as a drawer (existing), a full-width composer, and the canvas toolbar wrapping to two rows.

2. PROJECT (`project-home`): nav | page.
- Top: the project header (name, product, stage strip), then the start composer, "Start a conversation in ONC-221". It is the same AnaComposer, and it opens the conversation scoped to this project. This is Claude's project page.
- Below, at desktop width, two columns:
  - Main: Conversations (the existing list at ProjectHome.tsx:965-1027) and Documents (the project's authoring documents with status, sections drafted, owner and review state; each opens in the canvas).
  - A 320px side column: Files (project vault), Readiness, Tasks.
- 1100px and narrower: one column, in that order.
- No AnA card, and no rail.

3. AN OPEN DOCUMENT
- Phase 1: the conversation screen with the canvas open, reached from a turn, the Documents list or a hand-off.
- DocumentAuthoring remains as the full-width focus editor (nav | outline | page | side tabs). Its toolbar has "Discuss with AnA" instead of an AnA pane.
- Phase 2 (slice 13): DocumentAuthoring becomes the canvas's full-screen state.
- 1100px and narrower: side tabs float over the page (existing, authoring-v2.css:1653-1666).

4. VAULT, SUBMISSION CENTER, QUALITY, REPORTING AND EVERY OTHER SCREEN: nav | full-width page, with no right column.
- Record-level "Ask AnA about this" buttons hand off to the conversation, and the conversation's "Back to Vault" returns to the screen as it was left.
- 1100px and narrower: the nav becomes the 56px strip. 640px and narrower: drawer (existing).
design.anaPlacement:
WHERE: AnA is talked to in the conversation (`conversation-thread`, ConversationThread.tsx), in its centre column, and nowhere else.
- Home and the Project page carry the same composer component (AnaComposer, extracted from ConversationThread) in "start" mode. Typing there opens the conversation, as Claude's new-chat page and project page do.
- At any moment the person sees at most one AnA typing box.

WHY ONLY ONE: today there are four live conversations (S, W, E, R) and 8 composer locations.
- W, E and R start blank on every visit, and ⌘K, "Get help" and the "Conversation" nav entry go to a different thread from the pane on screen.
- One place gives one history, one context and one project scope, and a canvas that always sits on the same side.

THE RAIL (A1/A2, Shell.tsx:622-1548):
- Unmounted and deleted in slice 2.
- Its unique pieces are moved first, in slice 1:
  - "Working in" block → the conversation header chip.
  - First-run welcome starters → Home.
  - Engine picker → the conversation composer.
  - Live Drive tour/demo start → Home starters.
  - "What AnA can do here" chips → the screen's own buttons, plus the screen_actions AnA already receives in module_context. A governed act she proposes renders its Part 11 sign-off inline in the conversation (SignoffList, already mounted there).

IN-SURFACE DOCKS:
- Editor W (DocumentWorkbench.tsx:1419, pane 4533-4777): deleted in slice 6. The editor already hands every ask to its host when embedded. On DocumentAuthoring, "Discuss with AnA" opens the conversation with the same document and section in the canvas. The per-turn authoringContext the conversation already sends (ConversationThread.tsx:918-933, 4c8b5534) is exactly what W sent.
- eCTD E (EctdCoauthor.tsx:335, pane 794-923): deleted in slice 11. The co-author becomes tree | document. Its editor asks hand off with document and section context.
- RBM R (Rbm.tsx:160): left as it is, because RBM is locked out of the release (`LaunchScopeGate`) and no production client can reach it. tests/ui/one-shell.test.ts keeps it as a single dated exception, which expires when RBM enters scope.

HOME / PROJECT COMPOSERS:
- Home's own composer (Surfaces.tsx:264-402) and the ProjectHome "AnA · co-author" card (ProjectHome.tsx:902-937) are replaced by AnaComposer in start mode (slice 7). There is one composer implementation.

THE 77 "ASK AnA" BUTTONS: they all reach `V2App.ask` through `onAsk`, so one change routes all of them correctly (slice 2).
- `ask(text)` now hands off through the existing `window.C2C_CONVO` protocol, extended with `origin: { surfaceId, label, moduleContext }`.
- It navigates to the conversation and continues the current thread when that thread is in the same project; otherwise it starts a new one.
- It sends the request with the origin screen's published surface context as that turn's module_context and screenName (one new per-turn AnaSendOptions field, the same pattern as authoringContext).
- The user turn shows a "From Vault · <record>" chip, and the header offers "Back to Vault".
- Slices 9 and 10 then sort the buttons by one rule:
  - Buttons that name a job the screen can do become that action, about 10. Examples: BiopharmaProject "Open in editor" (:743) opens the editor; DispatchReadiness "Transmit" (:646) and "Fix" (:620) go to the Dispatch ceremony or open the item; Licensing "contact sales" (:104) becomes a request form; TaskBoard's unrequested auto-send (:1098) is removed; Vault "Ask AnA to import" (:1359) opens the import dialog.
  - Buttons with no context, about 5, are removed: Projects.tsx:1223, quality/App.tsx:290, Surfaces.tsx:497-503, TopBar and account "Get help".
  - The remaining record-scoped buttons, about 60, keep one label, "Ask AnA about this", and become context hand-offs.

KEPT AS KEYBOARD AND SYSTEM PATHS INTO THE SAME THREAD (none of them is a second place):
- ⌘K "Ask AnA" row.
- TaskTray "Triage my day".
- The Live Drive strip's steer box, shown only while AnA is driving another screen on this thread, now with "Back to conversation".
design.canvas:
WHAT IT IS: the right-hand column of the conversation, `.ct-canvas`.
- It replaces both today's side column (.ct-side: Progress plus the type-B Artifacts list, ConversationThread.tsx:1446-1478) and today's `.ct-canvas-pane`. Those two already occupy the same position and replace each other; they become one column with three states:
  - closed: nothing built and nothing opened, so the conversation is centred;
  - list: Documents;
  - open: one document in the one DocumentWorkbench (DocumentCanvas.tsx:597-631, unchanged).

LIVE BUILD WHILE AnA WRITES:
- Slice 3, client only: when `artifact_draft` carrying `authoringDocId` arrives mid-turn (useAnaChat.ts:1683-1717), the canvas opens on that document immediately rather than waiting for "Open full editor".
  - Sections AnA is still working on show "AnA is writing" until the turn settles.
  - The document re-reads on every completed tool step that names its id, not only when the turn ends.
  - It never takes over a canvas whose open document has unsaved edits. In that case the header shows "New document ready · Open".
- Slice 16, server: true streaming. stream.ts forwards the draft tool's partial input per section as `draft_progress` events. The canvas renders that text marked "being written, not saved" until the save event turns it into the stored record. The model's words are never shown as saved before they are.

LIST OF DOCUMENTS BUILT:
- "This conversation" reads `GET /api/authoring/docs?conversationId=` over the provenance AnA documents already carry (source 'ana', conversationId, turnId; ANA_DOCUMENT_CANVAS.md decision 4). This needs no migration.
  - Because the list is read from the server, it survives a reload. That structurally fixes the case where the 180-character tool-trace cut (tool-trace.ts:68-101) drops `authoringDocId`.
- "This project" reads the same route with programId and a "Built by AnA" filter.
- Type-B drafts of this session appear in the same list, with "Open as document" (existing draftToDocument).
- Each row shows title, type, status, sections drafted N of M, updated time, Open, and Download working copy.
- In the transcript, each document is a compact chip: title, status, Open. The duplicate action row on the inline card (DocumentCanvas.tsx:528-593) goes, because the actions live once in the canvas.

OPEN AND EDIT IN PLACE:
- The same editor as Authoring, one section at a time, with outline, comments, history, sources, signatures, audit and project files.
- AnA never writes into the open document. Her answers arrive as tracked suggestions through `insertSuggestion` (52697e0c), and later as anchored proposals (row 50's `propose_section_edit`). The person accepts or rejects each one, and the AI-suggestion decision is chained.
- Every turn names the open document and section (4c8b5534).
- "Edit in Authoring" becomes "⤢ Full screen".

DOWNLOAD — two acts, one renderer (slice 5):
- (a) Working copy, .docx or .pdf, available in any state.
  - New `POST /api/authoring/docs/:docId/working-copy`. It renders through `renderAuthoringExport` with the working-draft statement on page one that vault filing already uses (authoring-file-to-vault.ts:22-26).
  - Filename suffix "— working copy"; version label `draft-<sha8>`.
  - One chained audit row, `authoring.document.working_copy`, recording actor, document, content SHA-256 and format. It writes no export-history row, so the Exports rail still lists only controlled acts.
- (b) Controlled export, Word / PDF / XML.
  - Unchanged: allowed only when FROZEN or APPROVED, with the signature manifest. The server still refuses with 409 otherwise (authoring.router.ts:5816-5840).
  - The three always-disabled buttons (AuthoringCreateExport.tsx:225-233) become one Download menu. Controlled export is disabled there, with the reason shown.
- This is a CPO decision under the founder's delegation, recorded in the slice-2 decision record: a marked, audited working copy is a convenience copy and not a record. The authoring store remains the system of record.

VERSIONS: the workbench History tab (existing). The canvas header shows the version and the last-saved time.

PART 11:
- Section saves keep the existing provenance requirement, version write and audit row.
- Freeze, approve and §11.50 e-sign keep their existing ceremony (meaning, reason, re-authentication) and run from the workbench filing bar inside the canvas.
- The Audit tab and "Download the record" are unchanged.
- The status pill is always visible, so a person never mistakes a draft for a sealed record.

TIES TO THE AUTHORING STORE AND THE VAULT:
- The canvas shows only the authoring store (`authoring_documents` / `authoring_sections`), the one document store under ANA_DOCUMENT_CANVAS.md.
- "File to vault" is the existing governed act: it renders, ingests and files with a SHA-256 and a chained audit row, as a working draft or as a sealed record, and says which.
- The workbench's Project files tab reads the project vault (`/api/c2c/project-vault/`).
- Vault's "Open in editor" (editorTarget) lands on the canvas in phase 2 (slice 13).
- Type-B drafts become authoring documents automatically in slice 17, which retires the `concept2cure_artifacts` document path.
- ci:canvas-path (scripts/ci/check-canvas-path.mjs) stays green throughout: thread mounts canvas, canvas mounts workbench, Authoring mounts workbench, the tool is registered, the workbench reads the vault and the file-to-vault route exists.
design.workflow:
FOLD INTO THE PROJECT AND THE DOCUMENT (stop being destinations; reachable by ⌘K until each is deleted with its replacement named by path):
- Project home → it becomes the project workspace: start composer, Conversations, Documents, Files, Readiness, Tasks.
- Document editor and authoring → the canvas.
- Program journey → the project's stage strip.
- Filings catalog → "Start a filing" on the project.
- Tasks and collaboration → the project's Tasks panel, the document's Tasks tab, and the TaskTray, which is the one personal inbox.
- Review and approval → the document's review tab in the canvas. The reviewer's "Open" lands on the document at its section, and signing happens there.
- Template library → the "New document" picker. The library page stays as an admin page.
- Regulatory workspace and Protocol development → documents in the canvas.
- Dossier map, eCTD compile, eCTD co-author, Publishing and Gateway transmittals → tabs of the project's sequence in Submission Center.
- Submission Readiness (dispatch readiness) → Submission Center's Readiness tab and the project's Readiness panel. The entitlement stays, so D2's "seven apps" still holds; it is a feature, not a destination.
- Artifacts Center → the canvas's "This project" documents and Vault.
- QMS records that carry a project (PF-16) → shown on the project.

REMAIN AS CROSS-PROJECT PLACES:
- Conversation: Home and Recents.
- Projects (portfolio).
- Vault (every record).
- Submission Center (every sequence).
- Quality (organisation QMS).
- Reporting (organisation analytics and compliance reports).
- Settings, in the account menu: Apps, AnA memory, Admin and access, Billing, Training, Audit trail and Part 11 console.

THE CLIENT'S PATH THROUGH A PROJECT:
1. Home, then open ONC-221 (or pick it in Recents).
2. On the project page, type "Draft the 2.5 Clinical Overview from our CSR and IB" into the start composer.
3. The conversation opens, scoped to ONC-221. AnA plans in the transcript.
4. The canvas slides in on the right as the document is created, and sections fill as she writes.
5. The client edits a section, accepts or rejects AnA's tracked suggestions, and asks follow-ups. Each turn names the open section.
6. Assign review: the reviewer gets a TaskTray item. Open lands them on the same document, in the canvas, at the section, where they comment and give their verdict.
7. The author freezes the document and e-signs with meaning and reason.
8. File to vault: the sealed record, with SHA-256.
9. Place into filing, then the project's sequence in Submission Center: compile, then the Readiness tab, then the dispatch ceremony with e-signature.
10. At any point the client can download a marked working copy for an offline read.
11. Any screen's "Ask AnA about this" returns to the same conversation with that record attached.

Agency correspondence stays outside the release, as today.
design.navigation:
LEFT NAV, top to bottom:
1. "New conversation": a primary button that goes to Home, the empty conversation.
2. Recents: the signed-in person's last 8 conversations, read from GET /api/chat/threads.
   - Scoped server-side to user_id. Today the unfiltered list (server/routes/chat/threads.ts:83-96) is organisation-wide, which would show colleagues' first messages.
   - The current project's threads are marked.
3. Projects (label changes from "Project management").
4. Vault.
5. Submission Center.
6. Quality (QMS). Today it has no nav entry.
7. Reporting (label changes from "Reporting & analytics").

BOTTOM: the account menu, which gains Client type (the one segment selector), Apps, AnA memory, Admin and access, Billing and usage, Training, and Sign out.

HOME: the logo goes to Home; today it goes to the document editor (Shell.tsx:293-306). Home is the new-conversation page: AnaComposer in start mode, client-type starters, the first-run welcome, and recent projects.

TOP BAR: breadcrumb (Project › Screen, with the root as a link), ⌘K, TaskTray (the one place for "My tasks" and "Needs my review"), and the account menu.

REMOVED FROM NAVIGATION:
- The Client categories section and the TopBar Client domain selector → account menu, Client type.
- Science & intelligence (no entries in scope).
- Explore:
  - AnA Command → ⌘K;
  - AnA memory, Apps catalog → account menu;
  - Artifacts Center → Vault and the canvas;
  - Conversation → New conversation and Recents.
- Quick access: Recent Documents → Recents and project Documents; My Tasks → TaskTray.
- "Tasking" → TaskTray "Open task board".
- TopBar and account "Get help".

Nav entries go from 12 buttons over 11 screens to 7 entries plus Recents, and there is one client-type selector.

risks: Asking from a work screen now leaves that screen. The person no longer sees Vault or Submission Center while AnA answers. Mitigations: the context is carried, so AnA sees what they saw; 'Back to <screen>' restores the screen, including its selection; and slices 13-15, with a later 'canvas hosts work' step, bring records into the canvas beside the conversation.

Live Drive: AnA can navigate away from the conversation, and the drive strip becomes the only view of her. The strip must carry 'Back to conversation', and the walk must be rehearsed before the beta demo.

Governed actions and context keyed to screenName: a hand-off turn on conversation-thread would otherwise lose the origin screen's screen_actions and authorisation scope. Slice 2 must send the origin's screenName with its module_context. The admin flows that expected the sign-off next to the admin screen (AdminAccess.tsx:40) must be walked.

Fourteen rail test files guard real behaviour: history, attachments, run control, continue, warnings, context honesty. Deleting them without mapping each one to a conversation-screen test would silently remove coverage. Slice 2's commit must list the old-to-new mapping.

Lane collisions are live:
- 019ZvHmh (Shell.tsx, ConversationThread.tsx, app-v2.css)
- 01Wcyqbq (canvas, DocumentCanvas, authoring.router.ts)
- 01TTTQ1h (DocumentWorkbench, ConversationThread, stream.ts)
- 01JNRgCK (navParams)
- untrailered `concept2cure` commits on the same files on 2026-10-05/06.
No lane owns the shell. One lane must claim this series on the board and rebase before each slice.

Precedent of reversal: a chat-first nav restructure was reverted the same day on 2026-07-28 ('the shipped navigation wins'), and on 2026-09-24 consolidation kept everything ('keep what came from the design kits'). The founder has now delegated the decision. The decision record (slice 2) and the shell-nav test (slice 12) must make the change durable. registryModel's 'GENERATED from the kit' header would otherwise invite a re-port that restores the old nav.

Working-copy download (slice 5) is a governance call. If the page-one marking is weak, a working copy could be mistaken for a controlled record. QA/RA should review the statement's wording and the filename before beta. The export route's 409 must stay pinned by its regression test.
Canvas auto-open can steal focus. It must never replace an open document with unsaved edits, and it must announce politely rather than move focus during a person's typing.
Width between 1100 and 1440px: with the nav open the editor page is about 530px. Slice 3's nav auto-collapse and slice 8's divider are needed before investor demos on laptops.

Recents privacy: the existing global /api/chat/threads list is organisation-wide, filtered by organisation only. Exposing it in the nav without the user_id scope (slice 12) would show colleagues' first messages.

eCTD co-author uses a separate store (coauthor_documents). Removing E before its editor registers an EditorBridge would lose the in-place insert loop. Slice 11 states that precondition, and its fallback is Copy, never a silent write.
RBM's own dock R remains as a dated exception. If RBM enters launch scope before it is folded in, the product has two AnAs again. The one-shell test exception must name that trigger.
Rule 2: each slice must name row D2 and file evidence. A slice that cannot show its failing-first test and a real-browser check reports itself as blocked, not done.
